title: Shopping, colors and prices

I can describe clothes and colors with the right agreement.
I can ask for a size, say what I want to try on and ask about payment.
I can use este, esse and aquele to point to things, and bargain politely.

dialogues.title: Na loja de roupas
dialogues.context: Camila is looking for pants in a clothing store. Rogério is the salesperson.

lines.speaker: Rogério
lines.pt: Boa tarde! O que você procura?
lines.en: Good afternoon! What are you looking for?

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: Eu queria uma calça preta.
lines.en: I'd like a pair of black pants.

lines.speaker: Rogério
lines.pt: Temos estas calças aqui. Qual tamanho você usa?
lines.en: We have these pants here. What size do you wear?

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: Eu uso M. Quanto custa essa calça?
lines.en: I wear M. How much does this pair of pants cost?

lines.speaker: Rogério
lines.pt: Essa custa cento e vinte reais.
lines.en: That one costs one hundred twenty reais.

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: E aquela calça azul, quanto é?
lines.en: And that blue pair over there, how much is it?

lines.speaker: Rogério
lines.pt: Aquela custa noventa reais.
lines.en: That one costs ninety reais.

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: Eu quero experimentar a azul.
lines.en: I want to try on the blue one.

lines.speaker: Rogério
lines.pt: O provador fica ali, ao lado da porta.
lines.en: The fitting room is over there, next to the door.

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: Obrigada!
lines.en: Thank you!

dialogues.title: Pagando no caixa
dialogues.context: Fernando wants to buy sneakers. Bianca works at the register of a shoe store.

lines.speaker: Fernando
lines.pt: Esse tênis branco, quanto custa?
lines.en: These white sneakers, how much do they cost?

lines.speaker: Bianca
lines.pt: Custa duzentos e cinquenta reais.
lines.en: They cost two hundred fifty reais.

lines.speaker: Fernando
lines.pt: Que caro! Tem desconto?
lines.en: That's expensive! Is there a discount?

lines.speaker: Bianca
lines.pt: À vista, tem dez por cento de desconto.
lines.en: If you pay in one go, there is a ten percent discount.

lines.speaker: Fernando
lines.pt: E parcelado?
lines.en: And in installments?

lines.speaker: Bianca
lines.pt: Em três vezes, sem desconto.
lines.en: In three payments, without a discount.

lines.speaker: Fernando
lines.pt: Eu levo à vista. Vocês aceitam cartão?
lines.en: I'll take it in one payment. Do you accept cards?

lines.speaker: Bianca
lines.pt: Aceitamos cartão, dinheiro e Pix.
lines.en: We accept cards, cash and Pix.

lines.speaker: Fernando
lines.pt: Eu pago com cartão. Meu número é quarenta e dois.
lines.en: I'll pay by card. My size is forty-two.

lines.speaker: Bianca
lines.pt: Perfeito. Aqui está o tênis.
lines.en: Perfect. Here are the sneakers.

dialogues.title: Na feira
dialogues.context: Carlos is at an outdoor craft market. He talks to Dona Rita, who sells handbags, and tries to get a better price.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.pt: Bom dia, Dona Rita! Quanto é esta bolsa?
lines.en: Good morning, Dona Rita! How much is this purse?

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.pt: Essa bolsa custa cem reais.
lines.en: This purse costs one hundred reais.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.pt: Está um pouco cara. Faz por oitenta?
lines.en: It's a bit expensive. Will you do it for eighty?

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.pt: Para você, faço por noventa.
lines.en: For you, I'll do ninety.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.pt: E se eu levo duas? Tem desconto?
lines.en: And if I take two? Is there a discount?

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.pt: Duas bolsas, cento e setenta reais.
lines.en: Two purses, one hundred seventy reais.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.pt: Fechado! Eu quero uma vermelha e uma marrom.
lines.en: Deal! I want a red one and a brown one.

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.pt: Aqui estão. Obrigada!
lines.en: Here you go. Thank you!

grammar.title: Demonstratives: este, esse, aquele
grammar.explanation:
Demonstratives point to things. In textbooks there are three levels of distance: este (this, close to me), esse (that, close to you) and aquele (that over there, far from both). The matching neutral words isto, isso and aquilo are used when you point to something without naming it: o que é isso?

In everyday Brazilian speech, esse and essa are used for both close and middle-distance things, and este and esta are mostly heard in writing or formal speech. So in a store you will usually hear essa calça for this pair of pants in your hand. Aquele and aquela are kept for things that are clearly far away: aquela calça azul, over there.

Demonstratives agree with the noun in gender and number: esse tênis, essa bolsa, esses sapatos, essas camisetas. They also contract with de and em: desse, dessa, nesse, nessa, daquele, naquela. Isto, isso and aquilo never change and never come with a noun.

examples.en: This T-shirt is cheap.
These shoes are expensive.
That blue coat over there is nice.
What is this?
I want that thing over there.

grammar.title: Numbers from 100 to 1,000,000 and prices
grammar.explanation:
The hundreds change according to the number: cem (exactly 100), cento (100 followed by more), duzentos, trezentos, quatrocentos, quinhentos, seiscentos, setecentos, oitocentos, novecentos. Use e between hundreds, tens and units: cento e vinte, duzentos e trinta e cinco. Mil (1,000) never changes: dois mil, dez mil. One million is um milhão and the plural is milhões: dois milhões de reais.

Brazilian money is the real, plural reais, and a hundredth of a real is a centavo. Brazilians write R$ 49,90 with a comma for the decimals and say quarenta e nove reais e noventa centavos. In shops people often shorten this to quarenta e nove e noventa.

To ask the price use quanto custa? for a single item, quanto custam? for several items, or the shorter quanto é? and quanto são? For a price that is temporary or a special offer, you may also hear quanto está? Brazilians usually say quanto está o quilo? for items sold by weight.

examples.en: The T-shirt costs fifty reais.

examples.pt: O tênis custa duzentos e cinquenta reais.
examples.en: The sneakers cost two hundred fifty reais.

examples.pt: A bolsa custa cento e vinte reais.
examples.en: The purse costs one hundred twenty reais.

examples.pt: O celular custa mil e quinhentos reais.
examples.en: The cell phone costs one thousand five hundred reais.
How much do these pants cost?

grammar.title: Colors and adjective agreement
grammar.explanation:
In Portuguese the color goes after the noun: uma saia preta, a black skirt. Color adjectives agree with the noun in gender and number, like other adjectives. Those that end in -o change to -a, -os and -as: branco, branca, brancos, brancas; preto, preta; vermelho, vermelha; amarelo, amarela.

Colors ending in -e, -l or -a with no change for gender only take number: verde, verdes; azul, azuis; cinza. Some colors that come from fruits or flowers, such as rosa and laranja, are often left unchanged in everyday speech: duas bolsas rosa, camisetas laranja. Marrom has no feminine form and its plural is marrons.

To say light or dark, add claro or escuro after the color: azul-claro, azul-escuro, verde-escuro. The whole color expression stays in the same form, whatever the noun: uma camisa azul-escuro, duas camisas azul-escuro. To ask what someone prefers, use qual: qual é a sua cor favorita?

examples.en: I want a black skirt.
The white sneakers are new.
She wears a dark blue dress.
The green T-shirts are cheap.

examples.pt: Qual é a sua cor favorita?
examples.en: What is your favorite color?

grammar.title: Asking questions: quanto, qual, quais
grammar.explanation:
Use quanto custa? to ask how much one thing costs and quanto custam? for several things. The short forms quanto é? and quanto são? are very common in shops. All of these take a noun after them: quanto custa essa calça? A different question is quanto está? when the price is today's price: quanto está o dólar hoje?

Qual means which or what and is used to choose among options. Its plural is quais. Qual always agrees in number with the thing: qual é o seu tamanho? but quais são os seus números? Use qual before a verb or before a noun in everyday speech: qual tamanho você usa?

To ask for something in a shop, say eu queria... (I would like...), which is polite, or eu quero... when you are sure. Add por favor if you want to be extra polite. To ask whether a shop accepts a form of payment, use aceitar: vocês aceitam Pix? The answer is aceitamos, sim, or não aceitamos.

rows: How much does this purse cost?
How much do these sneakers cost?
Quais são as suas cores favoritas?

examples.en: How much does this coat cost?
How much do these pants cost?
What is your shoe size?

culture.title: Pix, installments and bargaining
culture.text:
Brazil's instant payment system, Pix, is used everywhere: in shops, at street stalls and between friends. You pay by scanning a QR code or typing a key such as a phone number, and the money moves in seconds at no cost for people. Many small businesses prefer Pix to cash, so it is worth asking vocês aceitam Pix? before you pay.

Another common feature is parcelamento. Shops often let you pay in three, six or ten monthly installments, often with no interest, and prices are frequently displayed as, for example, em dez vezes de vinte reais. Paying à vista, meaning in one payment, often earns a discount, and asking tem desconto? is normal in most shops. At feiras, craft markets and street stalls, bargaining is accepted, and a polite faz mais barato? or um descontinho? is part of the game.

Clothes come in P, M, G and GG, which stand for pequeno, médio, grande and extra grande. Shoes use numbers in the Brazilian system, usually from 34 to 44, so check the number rather than guess from another country's sizes. Prices are shown with R$ and a decimal comma.
